newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice prices seen up on weather reports.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice prices seen up on weather reports.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are likely to rise next week on reports that bad weather might hit the crop in India, dealers said on Thursday.

One exporter said prices had firmed in Pakistan after U.S. rice futures rose in the past two days on fears that El Nino weather patterns, which have in the past caused drought or drought-like conditions in some Asian nations and Australia, could cut the world rice crop, particularly in India.

But Zahid Khawaja, a member of the Rice Exporters Association of Pakistan, said adverse weather was unlikely to affect Pakistan, where rice sowing was completed in April/May and harvesting was due in September/October.
"India is likely to become a net importer," Khawaja said. "Pakistan is expected to export a large quantity of rice to India (in the financial year beginning on July 1)."
Pakistan would have a good chance to sell super and ordinary basmati rice to India, Khawaja said.
Exporter Khalid Ghori of Matco Rice Processing said IRRI-6 prices had firmed this week due to short supply.

A Lahore-based dealer said basmati prices could rise on talk that the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan was exploring possible export of 10,000 tonnes to an unnamed country. Basmati super export prices were rising gradually, the dealer said.

An official of the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) said it taken no decision on four bids, the highest of which was $441 per tonne FOB, received on Monday for the sale and export of 5,000 tonnes of basmati variety Pak-7 1996/97 (July-June) rice containing seven percent broken.
Other bidders had quoted $437, $437 and $436.75 per tonne FOB. The RECP reinvited the bids after scrapping three bids for the same quantity last month, saying they were too low.
The RECP had 10 days to decide whether to accept any of the latest bids, the official said.
Pakistan exported 1.603 million tonnes of rice worth $431 million in the first 11 months of 1996/97 compared to 1.253 million worth $411 million in the same period a year ago.
In May, rice exports fell to 124,338 tonnes worth $37 million compared to 185,349 tonnes worth $48 million in April and 119,565 tonnes worth $38 million in May 1996.
